summary: Puye Ruins lookout, Santa Fe NF: considered 1927,35-ft Indian Service tower dated 1931 or 1932, abandoned 1951; very little remains.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower, 35 ft, with a 7- by 7-foot steel cab
facts.status_note: The tower was dismantled at an unknown date and its destination is unknown. The 2017 report says very little remains at the site.

staffing.status: staffed only in extreme conditions in the 1940s; unstaffed and reportedly abandoned by 1949

access.note: The site is beside the Puye ruins on Santa Clara Pueblo Reservation land. The attraction at the ruins is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, and runs guided tours. No source says whether tours pass the lookout spot.

facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Santa Fe National Forest (tower erected by the Indian Service)

events.note: Forest considered a new lookout at Puye Ruins to replace Guaje Lookout, in cooperation with the Indian Service and a tour operator. Telephone line work started that year.
Agreement with the Indian Service to share the cost of manning the site. It did not work out because the Indian Service did not hire a lookout. No tower yet.
Indian Service erected a 35-foot steel Aermotor LS-40 tower with a 7- by 7-foot steel cab. The report dates it to 1931 or 1932.
New agreement: the Forest would hire, train and supervise the Puye lookout, and provide the protractor, stand, map, telephone and living quarters.
By September 1940 the Forest had moved a 10- by 14-foot cabin to the site. The Forest also suggested closing Puye and moving it to Indian Peak; that move was delayed by the war.
A telephone line was built from the tower to the cabin.
Lookout unstaffed and reportedly abandoned. Aerial observation and reliance on the Los Alamos tower were substituted.
Forest moved the Puye cabin and Osborne firefinder to the new Clara Peak Lookout. The report says Puye Lookout was abandoned.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The report says the lookout was unstaffed and reportedly abandoned by 1949, and also dates the abandonment of Puye Lookout to 1951, when its cabin and firefinder were moved to Clara Peak. The story gives both dates and attributes each to the report.
The report gives the tower's erection as 1931 or 1932 and does not choose between them. The event is recorded as 1931 with that note.

notes_for_editor: History rests on one thorough agency report (2017), which footnotes its sources. Build year is 1931 or 1932 per the report. The record gives the county as Sandoval; the Wikipedia article on the ruins describes the land as Santa Clara Pueblo Reservation land near Espanola and was not used to settle the county. Check the county against the NRHP nomination for the ruins (ref 66000484) before publishing. Access: the lookout site is on pueblo land next to the ruins, and no source says whether the tours pass it. The report's description of remains is from 2017.
